edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Thanks the Chapter for forwarding his stored goods from Magdeburg to Prague at their own expense, noting the Emperor received this service with favour.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Acknowledges Duke Otto of Brunswick's requests, encloses a reply for him, and reports his instruments installed in an Italian-style house beside the Emperor's garden at Prague.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Reports his goods arrived in Bohemia and asks Rollenhagen to deliver the enclosed letter to the Dean, explaining that the earlier silence was due to pressing imperial duties.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Urges completion of the promised collation, asks what Master Oswald and the printer will undertake, and reports arranging instruments in a new house the Emperor can visit.

recipient: The Dean and Doctors of the Faculty of Medicine at Wittenberg
edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Declines the invitation to the medical doctoral promotion at Wittenberg, citing his obligations to install his astronomical instruments in a new house at Prague by imperial command.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Sets out the terms of their contract — two years of astronomical assistance with Imperial backing — and reviews grievances arising from his current situation in Bohemia.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Reports finding errors in his own calculations from Tycho's worked examples and marvels that Tycho's eclipse calculation of 10 July agrees with observation to within one arc-minute.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Uses Bopenhausen's return to greet the Landgrave, acknowledges the late Landgrave Wilhelm's past favour, and affirms his continued wish to be of service to Hesse-Kassel.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Reports receiving Bording's reply on 600 joachimsthalers owed by the Mecklenburg treasury, now held by Lucas Backmeister until Gödelmann's arrival.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Reports that Backmeister has received the 600 thalers owed and requests Meier to deliver the next 600 thalers to Gödelmann before his departure to Rostock.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Thanks Bille for redeeming a Holstein bond and requests him to ensure the 10,000-thaler principal is recovered from Mecklenburg rent-master Andreas Meier by April 1601.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Discusses Swedish and Livonian affairs and leaves to Sturtz's judgement what the late Chytraeus wished inserted in the Historiola, with Gödelmann carrying the relevant documents.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Acknowledges agreement on poems by Melissus and Brasch, noting that Gödelmann carries a copy of what Chytraeus wished to insert about his emigration from Denmark.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Requests more rigorous presentation of planetary hypotheses, specifying that Ptolemaic/Alphonsine and Copernican data each be used according to their own parameters.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Reports that Warszewicki did not arrive, expresses concern for Kepler's lack of a secure position, promises to seek astronomical tables, and sends works by Angelus.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Sends the Alphonsine Tables and a transcription of Methodius's Revelation, expressing admiration for Tycho's new solar and lunar calculation.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Writes via his son accompanying Anthony Sherley's Persian legation to Rome, thanks Magini for handling a confidential commission, and discusses Baldi of Urbino's proposed writing project.

edition_of_record: Bibliotheca mathematica
abstract: Introduces his son Tycho, accompanying Anthony Sherley's Persian legation to Italy, and commends him to the Grand Duke's favour.

edition_of_record: Magini, Tabulae primi mobilis (Venice 1604)
abstract: Explains delay in carrying out Tycho's undisclosed commission, citing reliance on third parties such as Sagredo and the press of domestic obligations.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Reports Gödelmann's arrival with word that Tycho received his poem fragment, and asks why the promised materials needed to continue the poem were not sent.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Reports Duke Charles's occupation of almost all Livonia, the Polish Diet's resolution to wage war for three years, and personal losses from these events.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Reports paying out 600 thalers to Gödelmann on Tycho's behalf, exchanging Belgian for imperial coin, and notes the other 600 thalers will be due at Easter.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Introduces the bearer as an experienced spagyrist and reports political news about Duke Charles of Sweden's dispute with Lübeck and the recent Polish Diet at Warsaw.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Advocates for publication of an unfinished horological work held by a widow, requesting Tycho's name and patronage to bring it to press.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Announces the planned wedding of his daughter Elisabeth Brahe to Frans Tengnagel at the Curtius house in Prague between Easter and Pentecost, and invites Rosenkrantz.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Reports persistent efforts to obtain imperial intercession through Vice-Chancellor Coraduz on behalf of Rosenkrantz's cousin, delayed by matters of greater state importance.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Reports the Emperor's continued imperial favour and the recent purchase of a large house for 10,000 thalers for his use and astronomical study.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Follows up on a request to have household goods moved from Lübeck to Hamburg and raises the matter of recovering money from the treasurer of the younger Mecklenburg princes.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Sends a copied excerpt on the history of astronomy and directs Brasch to Apian's Astronomicum Caesareum, Reinhold's tables, and Peucer's Sphaera for further sources, leaving composition of a poem to his discretion.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Thanks Bacmeister for transmitting 600 thalers in interest from the Mecklenburg treasurer and presses for repayment of the outstanding principal via Duke Ulrich's authority as guarantor.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Thanks Sturtz for writing and reports political and military news: the Wallachian's new vassal status under the Emperor, Báthory's invasion of Transylvania, and preparations for the renewed Hungarian war.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Announces the betrothal of his daughter Elisabeth Brahe to Frans Tengnagel and invites Duke Ulrich to the planned wedding between Easter and Pentecost.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Reports forwarding Petkum's reply via a student carrier, notes furnaces from Hamburg delayed by Elbe flooding, and encloses a prognostication on the Turkish war by Dethard Horst.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Relays his son's report that the Grand Duke dissuaded the Persian Legation leader from bringing the son to Rome, citing danger from rumours about Tycho already circulating in Italy.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Describes David Fabricius's visit and his observations, laments Fabricius's pastoral constraints, and reports the Bishop of Cologne's mission to the Emperor concerning election of a King of the Romans.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Complains of an unreceived letter and presses Meier for overdue repayment of 10,000 thalers and interest, noting the sum has been pledged to others and kinsman Eske Bille has given assurances.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Müller acknowledges completing one year of imperial-commanded service with Tycho at Prague and records his petition to the Emperor for an honorarium covering expenses and trouble.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Presses again for repayment of 10,000 thalers and interest from the young Mecklenburg dukes, noting Duke Ulrich's prior order to rent-master Meier at Easter has gone unfulfilled.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Inquires whether David Fabricius arrived safely after departing with fears about the dangers of the journey, and commends himself as a friend.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Confirms the 10,000 thalers owed to Tycho fell due at Easter, explains the rent-master's failure to secure promised funds at the last hour, and assures Eske Bille repayment will be arranged.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Recounts successive failed repayment deadlines for the 10,000 thalers owed by Mecklenburg, including the recently-passed Midsummer term, and presses Meier for immediate settlement.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Renews the demand for repayment of 10,000 thalers and interest from Mecklenburg, recounting the contract terms and the loss caused by failure to pay at the agreed Easter deadline.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Explains that the 10,000 thalers have been lying ready in Güstrow since before Midsummer, and that Tycho need only send to demand them against return of the issued bond.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Denies any application for 2,000 thalers at Doberan, reaffirms the earlier call-in of the 10,000 thalers, and recounts the failure of his servant to collect the sum at Easter.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Reports receiving Tycho Brahe's letter claiming 10,000 thalers were paid on St. John's Day, and denies knowledge of a 2,000-thaler demand at Duke Ulrich's court.

edition_of_record: Dreyer, Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (1913–29)
abstract: Encloses Eske Bille's letter on 10,000 thalers owed to Tycho Brahe, confirms the sum is ready, and questions a report of 5,000 thalers remitted to Prague.
